## Comparison of Approaches

Both traces solve the same 3-coloring problem on identical graphs. They diverge in color-assignment strategy: Trace 1 greedily picks B=Blue, D=Green, E=Green, G=Blue, then branches on F (Red vs Green); Trace 2 picks B=Green, D=Blue, E=Blue, G=Green, then does case analysis on H (Red vs Blue). Both find valid colorings without backtracking. Neither divergence leads to failure—one produces a solution with F=Red, the other with F=Red as well, just with Green/Blue swapped for several nodes.

Where they diverge most is in verification redundancy and alternative exploration. Trace 1 explores a full F=Green alternative coloring, confirms it works, then discards it—a CYCLE that pays off by confirming solution non-uniqueness but has no downstream effect on the final answer. Trace 2 explores H=Red (Case 1) as an alternative to H=Blue (Case 2), finds it valid, then later re-examines it for color-balance aesthetics before discarding it—also a CYCLE. Both traces also re-verify their solutions and re-derive adjacency lists multiple times, adding no new constraints.

Neither trace exhibits MUSE behavior; all reasoning stays grounded in the given graph.

## Trace 1 Annotations

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's check if F could be something else." end="Let's stick with this one." basis="Opens an alternative branch coloring F=Green instead of F=Red, fully derives a second valid 3-coloring, then explicitly eliminates it in favor of the first solution."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me verify the graph structure again just to be absolutely sure." end="This matches my derived adjacency list exactly." basis="Reconstructs the full adjacency list already built at the start of the trace, confirming it matches with no new information added."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's double check the C5 cycle again." end="So 3 colors are necessary." basis="Re-derives the same C5 cycle (A-B-H-F-I-A) already identified earlier, re-checking each edge and reaching the same conclusion."

## Trace 2 Annotations

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Case 1: H = Red." end="I'll just provide the first one I found, it's fine." basis="Opens an alternative branch with H=Red, fully derives a valid coloring, later re-examines it for color balance, then explicitly eliminates it in favor of the original H=Blue solution."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's check node E again." end="It seems valid." basis="Re-verifies every node's neighbors individually, duplicating the edge-by-edge check already completed in the full assignment verification."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's double check specific edges." end="C-F: C is Blue, F is Red. OK." basis="Re-checks a subset of edges already verified in the full assignment verification, adding no new constraints or information."
